chunks: Abu al-Husayn ibn Abi Jayyid al-Qummi narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Salih ibn Abi Salih, saying:

Some people asked me in the year two hundred and ninety to collect religious dues. I refused that request and wrote a letter seeking instructions. The answer came: 'In Ray is Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Arabi. He should deliver it to him, for he is from our men of trust.'

key_terms.مِنْ ثِقَاتِنَا: from our men of trust/reliable ones

ai.seo_question: Who was the trusted deputy in Ray appointed to handle religious dues in the late 3rd century AH?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the administrative structure of the Ghaybah al-Sughra, where the narrator, facing uncertainty in collecting religious dues, sought written guidance to appoint Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Arabi in Ray as a trusted deputy (thiqah). It underscores the practical application of the Imam's authority through designated agents during the period of minor occultation, ensuring the continuity of financial and religious administration.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 391 - Abul Husain Ibn Abi Jayyed Qummi narrated to us from Muhammad Ibn Hasan Ibn Walid from Muhammad Ibn Yahya Amir from Muhammad Ibn Ahmad Ibn Yahya from Salih Ibn Abi Salih, saying:

Some people asked me in the year two hundred and ninety to accept religious dues. I refused that request and wrote a letter, seeking instructions. The answer came, “In Ray is Muhammad Ibn Ja’far Arabi. He should deliver it to him, for he is from our men of trust.”
